title: Metric Depth Estimation from Arbitrarily Degraded Low-Resolution Depth Prompts
claim: One method turns inputs with many kinds of degraded guidance into clean, detailed outputs, showing broad robustness across conditions.
layout: 2 rows by 5 columns, input over output, degradation labels beneath
description: A gallery of five columns, each showing one degradation condition: Arbitrary Scale, Gaussian Noise, Gaussian Blur, Low-Bit Compression and Real-World Degradation. The top row has indoor RGB photos (kitchen, stovetop, chair by a filing cabinet, classroom, curtain with a plant). Each photo has a small inset at bottom right showing the degraded low-resolution depth prompt in a warm-to-cool colormap. These insets look blocky, noisy or blurry. A label reading 'Input' sits at the bottom left of the first photo. The bottom row shows the matching high-resolution depth maps from AdaDS. They are smooth and sharp, with clear object boundaries such as the chair, pot, table and plant. A pink 'AdaDS' label sits at the bottom left of the first output. Condition names are in plain text below each column. The eye goes first to the bright depth maps in the bottom row.
caption: Given an RGB image and an arbitrarily degraded low-resolution depth prompt, AdaDS adaptively places the intermediate noisy sample in a high-density region of a pre-trained depth diffusion prior, enabling zero-shot estimation of fine-grained high-resolution metric depth.
abstract: We propose AdaDS, an Adaptive Diffusion Sampling framework for prompted metric depth estimation, which estimates high-resolution metric depth from an image and an arbitrarily degraded low-resolution depth prompt. This setting is commonly studied as depth super-resolution, where existing methods typically regress depth directly without an explicit prior over high-quality depth, and thus often produce artifacts under severe or unseen degradations. In contrast, AdaDS exploits the contraction property of Gaussian smoothing: as noise accumulates in the forward diffusion process, the noisy distributions of degraded prompts and their high-quality counterparts converge toward an isotropic Gaussian prior, while the prompt content is gradually erased. Accordingly, AdaDS refines the prompt and estimates its uncertainty to adaptively select a starting timestep, and injects learned noise to place the intermediate sample in a high-density region of the depth distribution learned by a pre-trained diffusion model. Denoising from this sample yields high-quality depth with fine-grained details and corrects residual errors, even under imperfect prompt refinement. Experiments on real-world and synthetic benchmarks demonstrate its superior zero-shot generalization and robustness to diverse degradations.
